subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw commit to a supported external, non-Node agent-runtime ABI for embedded or bare-metal ports, and if so what minimum capability and compatibility contract should it guarantee?
rationale: The request adds a major platform and public-contract commitment rather than repairing an established behavior; source and roadmap evidence do not define the supported runtime boundary or long-term compatibility policy.

options.title: Defer a stable portable ABI
options.body: Keep OpenClaw's supported runtime Node-hosted for now and allow independent ports to experiment without an OpenClaw compatibility promise.

options.title: Sponsor a scoped protocol RFC
options.body: Define a deliberately small versioned agent-loop and capability protocol with conformance tests before accepting an embedded reference implementation.

options.title: Treat it as an external port
options.body: Encourage MimiClaw-style projects to remain separate implementations rather than claiming OpenClaw runtime compatibility.

recommendation.title: Defer a stable portable ABI
recommendation.body: Keep OpenClaw's supported runtime Node-hosted for now and allow independent ports to experiment without an OpenClaw compatibility promise.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged agent-runtime refactor and the existing discussion connect this person most directly to the current runtime boundary and its possible evolution.
